newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Tourist plane crash in Senegal kills at least 23.
newsitem.headline: Tourist plane crash in Senegal kills at least 23.

text.p: A plane carrying tourists back from a hunting party in a game park in Senegal crashed on takeoff killing at least 23 people, most of them French nationals, state television reported.

The son of the president of neighbouring Guinea Bissau, a co-pilot on the Air Senegal charter flight from the central town of Tambacouda, was also among the dead, it said. A further 29 people were injured.
State radio said earlier that the plane crashed on Saturday on leaving Tambacouda for the former French colony's capital of Dakar, 450 km (280 km) away.
"After taking off the aircraft crashed on the tarmac and burst into flames," a witness told Dakar Radio. He said the injured were thrown clear when the plane hit the runway.
Tambacouda is the airport for the Nioko Lo-Koba game park, which park has a wide range of animals including lions but hunting is limited to buffalo and deer.
Officials said most of the dead appeared to be French but that some might have been Belgian with possibly one Italian.
The television said two Senegalese crew members and Vladimir Vieira, a pilot with Air Senegal and son of President Joao Bernardo Vieira of Guinea Bissau, were also killed.

Senegal, particularly its separatist southern province of Casamance, is a favourite holiday destination for tourists from France and Germany. African Americans on tours in search of their roots are also frequent visitors.

Two French couples disappeared while on holiday in Casamance in 1995. Despite extensive searches in and around the combat zone where troops and separatist rebels occasionally clash neither the tourists nor their bodies have been found.
